item.title: Augusta judgeship finalists narrowed to two
item.description: Two Augusta lawyers have made the short list for Gov. Brian Kemp’s upcoming appointment to the Augusta Circuit bench. The post Augusta judgeship finalists narrowed to two appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Notre Dame and USC pause their longstanding rivalry, Fighting Irish add BYU to 2026 schedule
item.description: Notre Dame vs. Southern California, one of college football's biggest and longest rivalries, is on pause. The post Notre Dame and USC pause their longstanding rivalry, Fighting Irish add BYU to 2026 schedule appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Kansas City Chiefs announce they will leave Arrowhead and relocate across the Kansas-Missouri border
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs announced Monday they will leave their longtime home at Arrowhead Stadium for a new, domed stadium that will be built across the Kansas-Missouri state line and be ready for the start of the 2031 season. The post Kansas City Chiefs announce they will leave Arrowhead and relocate across the Kansas-Missouri border appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: No. 2 Georgia is trying to make the most of its break before CFP quarterfinal against No. 6 Ole Miss
item.description: Kirby Smart said Monday he has tried to use a long break to help No. 2 Georgia prepare for its College Football Playoff quarterfinal game against No. 6 Mississippi in the Jan. 1 Sugar Bowl. The post No. 2 Georgia is trying to make the most of its break before CFP quarterfinal against No. 6 Ole Miss appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Two Augusta-area lottery players score big as Powerball jackpot climbs to $1.6 billion
item.description: Two lottery players from the Augusta area were among several Georgians who won major prizes in the December 20 Powerball drawing. The Powerball jackpot has now surged to an estimated $1.6 billion. item.title: Local Christian school for students with special needs look toward expanding
item.description: Apparo Academy, a non-profit private school geared toward children with special needs, is planning an expansion at its west Augusta location, to include land owned by the Plunkett Family Revocable Trust. The post Local Christian school for students with special needs look toward expanding appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Black leaders group honors Augusta officials

item.title: Salvation Army of Augusta calls for last minute support to meet $50,000 gap
item.description: With just two days of bell-ringing left, The Salvation Army of Augusta is asking residents to help raise the remaining $50,000 left to meet its 2025 Red Kettle Campaign goal.
